claims.text: The headline outcome of an execution is exactly one word from the frozen outcome set of spec section 7, assigned on the primary fit by the comparison rule of spec section 5.

evidence.description: Spec 053 sections 4.3-4.5 as frozen, read first-hand at this draft: the comparison rule (fits as well iff error at or below the Indus error; the synthetic median rule; the NEAR MISS reporting band), the positive-control validity condition, and the three headline words.

Spec 053 adjudication section 8: DD-053-15 confirms the comparison rule with epsilon = 0 and the 0.02 band reporting-only; DD-053-19 confirms COMPARISON UNINFORMATIVE as the positive-control-failure class.

alternatives: a tolerance band inside the verdict rule (refused at Spec 053, DD-053-2: the design's words carry no band; the 0.02 band survives as the reporting-only NEAR MISS rule, so a near miss is named, not buried, and decides nothing)

claims.text: The sensitivity fit is reported alongside the primary fit in full (spec section 6.1).

evidence.description: Amendment S-053, readiness assessment section 1.5, quoted in spec section 2.1: the sensitivity fit over 5,299 rows (5,131 analyzable) is reported alongside the primary; if the two fits' verdict-relevant ordering against the controls differs, both are reported and neither is suppressed; rows graded undocumented-uncorroborated (405) enter no fit. Proposal P-F1 S4 (section 1.6): a result that changes between the two grade sets is reported as grade-sensitive wherever it is cited.

Provenance audit sections 2 and 4, read first-hand at this draft: the unmatched/corroborated stratum differs systematically from the documented stratum (45.1% incomplete against 6.7%; 45.2% containing a 000 placeholder against 7.3%; mean length 3.13 signs against 3.79), and undocumented-uncorroborated rows are graded not usable for load-bearing work.

alternatives: reporting only the combined fit because it is larger (refused: its population differs by construction, and P-F1 S4 requires both-ways reporting of any load-bearing result computed over both grade sets)
letting a differing sensitivity ordering silently replace the primary headline (refused: the headline is the primary's, with the grade-sensitivity statement carried beside it)
falsification_tests: the outcome record either reports both fits in full with both orderings, or it does not comply; a product quoting the headline without the grade-sensitivity statement where the orderings differ, or in which any undocumented-uncorroborated row entered a fit or count, falsifies compliance

evidence.description: Proposal P-F1 S3, readiness assessment section 1.6, read first-hand at this draft, quoted verbatim in this claim: every product of a citing spec states the lineage statement in its headline block; a product without the statement does not cite the corpus.

Provenance audit section 3 caveat, read first-hand at this draft - the statement's source in substance: Shakti and the program's lineage layer all descend from ICIT; their agreement is consistency within one tradition, not independent corroboration (the audit's census found the first 5,679 Shakti rows agree sequence-for-sequence with the lineage layer).

evidence.description: Amendment S-053, readiness assessment section 1.5, quoted in spec section 2.1: 'The V3 / Mahadevan-lineage corpus, the Phase-43 census (3,916 / 3,137 / 12,494), and the Phase-43 exponent are not inputs to this spec and no quantity in it is a reproduction of a Phase-43 quantity.' alternatives: reporting the Shakti exponent beside the Phase-43 exponent so a reader can see whether it 'still' holds (refused: in a different numbering, over a different population, the comparison would present a new baseline as a reproduction - exactly what Amendment S-053 and decision 2c exclude)
